# magpie-websearch

[中文说明](README.md) | [English](README.en.md) Additional web search APIs for [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai). Once installed, the APIs appear in **Settings › Models › Web search**, where Magpie manages keys, on/off switches and request order. The plugin registers **21 search channels**: AnySearch, Bocha, Jina, Kagi, Keenable, Linkup, Metaso, Moonshot, Moonshot CN, Ollama, Parallel, Perplexity, Querit, SerpApi, Serper, StepFun, TinyFish, plus separate Standard REST and Coding Plan MCP channels for Z.ai and Zhipu. AnySearch, Keenable, Parallel and TinyFish support keyless anonymous access; the other seventeen require the key for their specific product. ## Install ```sh magpie plugin add @guotree/magpie-websearch # Or install from GitHub magpie plugin add github:guotree/magpie-websearch ``` ## Quick start In Magpie's **Settings › Models › Web search**, add the APIs you want, switch them on and set their order. Leave the key empty for APIs that support anonymous access, or supply a key to use your account. You can also add APIs from the terminal: ```sh # Keyless anonymous search magpie search add magpie-websearch:anysearch # Use your own API key magpie search add magpie-websearch:linkup # List search APIs magpie search ``` All twenty-one APIs are registered by default without plugin options. Magpie's Web search settings determine which APIs are used. Since Magpie v0.1.3062, agents can specify `count` when calling `web_search` (1–20, default 6). From the terminal: ```sh magpie tool web_search "OpenAI API documentation" --count 20 ``` Without a configured result limit, the plugin follows the host's `count`, subject to each provider's limits. All providers use the optional `resultLimit` or `*_RESULT_LIMIT` environment variable for a user cap. Providers may return fewer results; the plugin makes no extra requests to fill them. Legacy names remain compatible; see [migration and count policy](docs/technical-reference.en.md#configuration). Leave **Base URL** empty for official services. A custom address must be the complete endpoint; the plugin does not append paths. See [Custom Base URL](docs/technical-reference.en.md#custom-base-url). To adjust provider parameters, use **Plugins → Installed → Options**, or run: ```sh magpie plugin options magpie-websearch '{"anysearch":{"format":"markdown"}}' ``` The Options editor starts from the package's AnySearch example. It is not applied until you click Save; the example uses AnySearch's default `format`, so saving it changes no behavior. Each command replaces the complete saved options object, so include every option you want to keep. Saving reloads the plugin host. See the [technical reference](docs/technical-reference.en.md#configuration) for all parameters and registration filters. ## Supported providers | Provider | Vendor ID | Key | Main capabilities | |---|---|---|---| | AnySearch | `magpie-websearch:anysearch` | optional | Intent routing, `cn`/`intl` zones, Markdown/JSON output | | Bocha | `magpie-websearch:bocha` | required | Standalone China REST search, snippet default with optional generated summary, freshness filters | | Jina | `magpie-websearch:jina` | required | Dedicated Jina Search endpoint, snippet default with optional full text truncation and publishedTime | | Kagi | `magpie-websearch:kagi` | required | Kagi Search API in public preview, with Lens, recency, and region filters | | Keenable | `magpie-websearch:keenable` | optional | Anonymous or keyed search, `pro`/`realtime` modes | | Linkup | `magpie-websearch:linkup` | required | Query-relevant excerpts with four search depths | | Metaso | `magpie-websearch:metaso` | required | Metaso search with scopes such as webpages and papers | | Moonshot | `magpie-websearch:moonshot` | required | Basic search on international site, snippet default with optional full text | | Moonshot CN | `magpie-websearch:moonshot-cn` | required | Basic search on domestic site, snippet default with optional full text | | Ollama | `magpie-websearch:ollama` | required | Cloud Web Search API using an Ollama account key, configurable content length | | Parallel | `magpie-websearch:parallel` | optional | Anonymous MCP (`fast`) or keyed REST; up to 20 results | | Perplexity | `magpie-websearch:perplexity` | required | Standalone Search API, `web`/`fast` modes, recency and country/language filters | | Querit | `magpie-websearch:querit` | required | Snippets or sentence-level matches | | SerpApi | `magpie-websearch:serpapi` | required | Google organic search with geography, language and safe-search settings | | Serper | `magpie-websearch:serper` | required | Alternative Google organic search, single-page 10 results, geography, language and tbs filters | | StepFun | `magpie-websearch:stepfun` | required | Standalone China REST search with scenario preferences and snippet/full text selection | | TinyFish | `magpie-websearch:tinyfish` | optional | Anonymous MCP or keyed REST; web, news and papers (papers require a key) | | Z.ai | `magpie-websearch:zai` | required | Standalone REST search on Zhipu's international site using `search-prime` | | Z.ai Coding Plan | `magpie-websearch:zai-coding` | required | International Coding Plan search over Streamable HTTP MCP; consumes shared plan credits | | Zhipu | `magpie-websearch:zhipu` | required | Standalone REST search on the China site with `search_std`/`search_pro`, Sogou and Quark engines | | Zhipu Coding Plan | `magpie-websearch:zhipu-coding` | required | China Coding Plan search over Streamable HTTP MCP; consumes shared plan credits | Search entries appear as ` (magpie-websearch)` in Magpie. Vendor IDs remain `magpie-websearch:`; plugin options and registration filters use short IDs such as `linkup`. See [PROVIDERS.md](PROVIDERS.md) for full support status and the integration plan. ## Privacy and security - **Direct endpoints**: Requests go directly to official vendor APIs or an explicitly configured custom endpoint. - **Search data and protocol metadata**: Requests contain search parameters; MCP initialization also includes the client name, package version and protocol capabilities. Conversation history, system prompts, user files, tool outputs and agent context are never read or forwarded. - **Magpie manages credentials**: Keys are sent using each vendor's protocol. SerpApi errors omit original exceptions, response bodies and request URLs; other providers retain their own diagnostic handling. The plugin cannot control vendor or proxy access logs. - **No silent downgrade**: Failed keyed requests never downgrade to anonymous access. - **Strict channel isolation**: Coding Plan keys and Standard API keys are not interchangeable. A provider never turns an MCP failure into metered REST or an automatic retry on the other site. Magpie may try another explicitly configured provider in order, using that provider's own key. The two Coding Plan providers are currently experimental. The official pages describe a Remote MCP for compatible clients but do not list Magpie as an officially supported client. Confirm the Coding Plan usage policy and your account terms before use; this project does not claim official Zhipu or Z.ai support for Magpie. Leaving the key empty while editing an existing keyed entry keeps its saved key. See [Anonymous search and rate limits](docs/technical-reference.en.md#anonymous-search) for switching back to anonymous access and handling rate limits. ## Detailed documentation | Topic | Contents | |---|---| | [Custom Base URL](docs/technical-reference.en.md#custom-base-url) | Exact endpoints, URL validation and MCP/REST switching | | [CLI management](docs/technical-reference.en.md#cli) | Adding APIs, multiple keys, ordering, switches and removal | | [Anonymous search and rate limits](docs/technical-reference.en.md#anonymous-search) | Anonymous endpoints, access-mode switching, 429 cooldowns and fallback | | [Provider protocols](docs/technical-reference.en.md#parallel-search) | Endpoints, capability limits and verification records for Parallel, [TinyFish](docs/technical-reference.en.md#tinyfish-search), [SerpApi](docs/technical-reference.en.md#serpapi-search), [Moonshot](docs/technical-reference.en.md#moonshot-search), [Zhipu and Z.ai](docs/technical-reference.en.md#zhipu-search), [StepFun](docs/technical-reference.en.md#stepfun-search), [Perplexity](docs/technical-reference.en.md#perplexity-search), [Bocha](docs/technical-reference.en.md#bocha-search), [Ollama](docs/technical-reference.en.md#ollama-search), [Jina](docs/technical-reference.en.md#jina-search), [Kagi](docs/technical-reference.en.md#kagi-search), and [Serper](docs/technical-reference.en.md#serper-search) | | [Result processing](docs/technical-reference.en.md#result-processing) | Result counts, text cleanup, dates and error statuses | | [Full configuration reference](docs/technical-reference.en.md#configuration) | Options, environment variables, precedence, caching and timeouts | | [Registration filters](docs/technical-reference.en.md#registration-filters) | `enable`/`disable` rules and examples | | [Development and local tests](docs/technical-reference.en.md#development) | Node/Bun, Magpie host tests, sandboxing and verified versions | ## Roadmap The third batch of planned standalone web search APIs (Jina, Kagi, Serper) has now been fully integrated; see [PROVIDERS.md](PROVIDERS.md#planned) for the integration plan. A model provider preset or a model's built-in search capability alone does not exclude a vendor's standalone search API from consideration. Official search support is checked before adding a new integration. Both Coding Plan implementations and local simulations are complete. Real-key search, plan-credit versus Standard REST billing checks, and confirmation of the client policy for Magpie remain pending. Experimental support does not imply real-account verification. ## Acknowledgements Provider adapters and response fixtures were initially based on [guotree/opencode-search-plugin](https://github.com/guotree/opencode-search-plugin) v4.6.1. ## License MIT ## Friend Links - [LINUX DO](https://linux.do/) — the new ideal community

# magpie-websearch

[中文说明](README.md) | [English](README.en.md) 为 [magpie](https://usemagpie.ai) 增加的第三方多源网页搜索 API 插件。安装后，这些 API 会出现在 **设置 › 模型 › 网页搜索** 中，由 Magpie 统一管理密钥、启用开关与请求顺序。 支持 **21 个搜索通道**：AnySearch、Bocha、Jina、Kagi、Keenable、Linkup、Metaso、Moonshot、Moonshot CN、Ollama、Parallel、Perplexity、Querit、SerpApi、Serper、StepFun、TinyFish，以及 Z.ai／Zhipu 各自独立的标准 REST 与 Coding Plan MCP。AnySearch、Keenable、Parallel 和 TinyFish 支持免 Key 匿名访问；其余十七个通道需要对应产品的 Key。 ## 安装 ```sh magpie plugin add @guotree/magpie-websearch # 或从 GitHub 安装 magpie plugin add github:guotree/magpie-websearch ``` ## 快速上手 在 Magpie 的 **设置 › 模型 › 网页搜索** 中添加需要的 API，开启并调整顺序。支持匿名访问的 API 可以留空 Key；填写 Key 则使用自己的账户。 也可以通过命令行添加： ```sh # 免 Key 匿名搜索 magpie search add magpie-websearch:anysearch # 使用自己的 API Key magpie search add magpie-websearch:linkup # 查看搜索 API magpie search ``` 默认注册全部 21 个 API，无需设置插件选项。Magpie 的网页搜索设置决定实际使用哪些 API。 Magpie v0.1.3062 起，Agent 可在调用 `web_search` 时指定 `count`（1–20，默认 6）；命令行示例： ```sh magpie tool web_search "OpenAI API documentation" --count 20 ``` 插件未配置数量上限时跟随宿主 `count`，并遵守各供应商限制；所有供应商统一使用可选的 `resultLimit` 或 `*_RESULT_LIMIT` 环境变量设置用户上限。供应商可能返回更少结果，插件不追加请求补足条数。旧选项保留兼容，迁移与数量策略见[技术参考](docs/technical-reference.md#configuration)。 使用官方服务时，将 **Base URL** 留空；自定义地址应填写完整端点，插件不会追加路径。详见[自定义 Base URL](docs/technical-reference.md#custom-base-url)。 如需调整供应商参数，可在 **Plugins → Installed → Options** 配置，或运行： ```sh magpie plugin options magpie-websearch '{"anysearch":{"format":"markdown"}}' ``` Options 编辑器会用包内的 AnySearch 示例预填；示例不会自动生效，点击 Save 后才会写入并重载。示例使用 AnySearch 的默认 `format`，保存后行为不变。 每次命令会替换已保存的完整选项对象，需包含希望保留的所有选项。保存后插件宿主会自动重载。完整参数和注册过滤见[技术参考](docs/technical-reference.md#configuration)。 ## 支持的供应商 | 供应商 | Vendor ID | Key 需求 | 主要能力 | |---|---|---|---| | AnySearch | `magpie-websearch:anysearch` | 可选 | 意图路由、`cn`／`intl` 分区、Markdown／JSON 输出 | | Bocha | `magpie-websearch:bocha` | 必填 | 博查中文搜索，默认普通摘要、可选生成摘要与时效筛选 | | Jina | `magpie-websearch:jina` | 必填 | Jina Search 专用端点，默认摘要、可选全文正文截断与时效映射 | | Kagi | `magpie-websearch:kagi` | 必填 | Kagi Search API 公开 Preview，支持 Lens、时间与地区过滤 | | Keenable | `magpie-websearch:keenable` | 可选 | 匿名或带 Key 搜索，支持 `pro`／`realtime` 模式 | | Linkup | `magpie-websearch:linkup` | 必填 | 查询相关摘录，支持四档检索深度 | | Metaso | `magpie-websearch:metaso` | 必填 | 秘塔搜索，支持网页、论文等搜索范围 | | Moonshot | `magpie-websearch:moonshot` | 必填 | 国际站 Basic 网页搜索，默认摘要、可选页面正文 | | Moonshot CN | `magpie-websearch:moonshot-cn` | 必填 | 国内站 Basic 网页搜索，默认摘要、可选页面正文 | | Ollama | `magpie-websearch:ollama` | 必填 | Ollama 官方云端网页搜索，需账户 API Key，支持本地正文截断 | | Parallel | `magpie-websearch:parallel` | 可选 | 匿名 MCP（`fast`）或带 Key REST；最多 20 条 | | Perplexity | `magpie-websearch:perplexity` | 必填 | 官方独立 Search API，支持 `web`／`fast` 模式、时效与国家／语言筛选 | | Querit | `magpie-websearch:querit` | 必填 | 摘要或句子级匹配内容 | | SerpApi | `magpie-websearch:serpapi` | 必填 | Google 自然搜索，支持地区、语言和安全搜索配置 | | Serper | `magpie-websearch:serper` | 必填 | Google 自然搜索备用渠道，当前单页 10 条、支持地区语言与 tbs 筛选 | | StepFun | `magpie-websearch:stepfun` | 必填 | 阶跃星辰国内站独立 REST 搜索，支持场景偏好、摘要／正文选择 | | TinyFish | `magpie-websearch:tinyfish` | 可选 | 匿名 MCP 或带 Key REST；网页、新闻和论文搜索（论文需 Key） | | Z.ai | `magpie-websearch:zai` | 必填 | 智谱国际站独立 REST 搜索，使用 `search-prime` | | Z.ai Coding Plan | `magpie-websearch:zai-coding` | 必填 | 国际站 Coding Plan 的 Streamable HTTP MCP 搜索，消耗套餐共享 credits | | Zhipu | `magpie-websearch:zhipu` | 必填 | 智谱国内站独立 REST 搜索，支持 `search_std`／`search_pro`、搜狗和夸克引擎 | | Zhipu Coding Plan | `magpie-websearch:zhipu-coding` | 必填 | 国内 Coding Plan 的 Streamable HTTP MCP 搜索，消耗套餐共享积分 | 搜索项在 Magpie 中显示为 ` (magpie-websearch)`。Vendor ID 保持为 `magpie-websearch:`；插件选项和注册过滤使用 `linkup` 等短 ID。完整支持状态与接入规划见 [PROVIDERS.md](PROVIDERS.md)。 ## 隐私与安全 - **直连端点**：请求直接发往厂商官方 API，或用户显式配置的自定义端点。 - **搜索数据与协议元信息**：请求包含搜索参数，MCP 握手另含客户端名称、包版本及协议能力；不读取或转发对话记录、系统提示词、用户本地文件、工具输出或 Agent 上下文。 - **Magpie 管理凭证**：Key 按厂商协议传递。SerpApi 错误省略原始异常、响应体和请求 URL；其他厂商保留各自的诊断处理。插件不能控制厂商或代理的访问日志。 - **不静默降级**：带 Key 的请求失败时，不会降级为匿名访问。 - **通道严格隔离**：Coding Plan Key 与 Standard API Key 不通用；provider 内部不会将 MCP 失败改走按次计费 REST，或自动跨站重试。Magpie 可按用户显式配置的顺序尝试其他 provider，各自使用自己的 Key。 两个 Coding Plan provider 目前标记为实验性接入：官方页面说明 Remote MCP 可用于兼容客户端，但未明确把 Magpie 列为官方支持客户端。使用前请自行确认 Coding Plan 使用政策与账户条款；本项目不声称 Magpie 获得智谱或 Z.ai 官方支持。 已有 Key 的条目编辑时留空 Key，仍会保留原 Key。切回匿名访问的方法及限流处理见[匿名搜索与限流](docs/technical-reference.md#anonymous-search)。 ## # Providers

This plugin adds search services to magpie. It targets standalone web search
APIs that magpie has not already integrated in the official source reviewed
below; all third-batch candidates (Jina, Kagi, Serper) have now been integrated.
A model provider preset alone does not cover a vendor's standalone search API.

Every search definition's `name` must follow `<Provider> (magpie-websearch)`.
This suffix identifies the plugin in magpie's GUI and CLI. Keep the short API ID
and the namespaced vendor ID independent of the display name; suffix changes
must not rename the IDs used by saved keys, switches, order or plugin options.

All twenty-one APIs are registered by default. `enable` and `disable` are optional
plugin options that filter this list by short ID (`linkup`, for example).
`disable` takes precedence over `enable`; `enable: []` registers none, while
`disable: []` excludes none. Provider settings such as `linkup.depth` do not
restrict registration by themselves. magpie manages keys, request order and
on/off switches for the registered APIs. See the [registration filters reference](docs/technical-reference.en.md#registration-filters)

authentication headers; Keenable selects the `/public` endpoint and sends

selects POST `https://api.parallel.ai/v1/search` with `x-api-key` for Parallel, or
GET `https://api.search.tinyfish.ai/` with `X-API-Key` for TinyFish; failures do not
downgrade to anonymous. Anonymous 429 cooldowns are maintained per API instance and
final endpoint, respecting `Retry-After` with a 60-second default. Keyed requests
and other endpoints are independent of that cooldown. See
[anonymous search reference](docs/technical-reference.en.md#anonymous-search) for setup and switching modes.

### Parallel protocol notes

- The [Search API reference](https://docs.parallel.ai/api-reference/search/search.md)
  describes GA POST search at `/v1/search`. Beta `/v1beta/search` and deprecated top-level
  `max_results`, `excerpts` and `processor` fields are avoided.
- Anonymous MCP was verified on **2026-11-04**: `web_search` over SSE returned HTTP 200
  without credentials or cookies for English and Chinese queries. `tools/list` requires
  `objective` and `search_queries`; the adapter populates both from the normalized query.
- Parallel defaults to `fast` mode on MCP and for agents. REST supports `fast`, `turbo`,
  `basic` and `advanced`. Non-`fast` modes require an API key and fail with a clear
  message if run anonymously.
- Public search caps results at 20. The adapter sizes requests with `resolveResultCount(count, countPolicy)`.
- Excerpts are joined with `\n\n`; text retains up to `contentChars` code points
  (default 4000, 0 keeps all) and appends `…` when truncated. `publish_date` maps to `age`.
- Custom Base URLs are exact endpoints for either mode without automatic path rewriting.

### TinyFish protocol notes

- The [REST reference](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/search-api/reference.md) and
  [OpenAPI](https://agent.tinyfish.ai/v1/openapi/search) describe authenticated GET
  search. The default endpoint is the product host's root, with no `/v1/search`.
- Anonymous MCP was verified on **2026-11-04**: the keyless header produced HTTP
  200 search results without a key, OAuth token or cookies. Omitting it produced
  401; adding it to REST still produced 401. `tools/list` advertised `web` and
  `news`, including location, language and domain filters. `research_paper` is
  keyed-only. Anonymous quotas and long-term availability are not guaranteed by
  this observation; the [MCP guide](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/mcp-integration/index.md)
  primarily documents OAuth.
- A single stateless `tools/call` works without `initialize`. Responses may be
  JSON or SSE. Its transport is implemented in
  [mcp/stateless.mjs](src/mcp/stateless.mjs), not a general MCP client.
  Search JSON is extracted from `structuredContent.results` or
  JSON text in `content[]`; JSON-RPC and tool failures are errors, not empty hits.
  RPC codes do not become numeric HTTP statuses.
- Both paths return one page without a count parameter. Filter missing URLs,
  preserve array order, then cap locally. Map `snippet` to `text` and string
  `date` to `age`; do not turn a paper's numeric year into a date.
- Custom Base URLs are complete endpoints, used as given for MCP POST without a
  key or REST GET with one. No path is appended. A mode change may require a new
  custom address. Caches include mode, endpoint, effective parameters/count and key.
- First-version settings expose geography, language, search type and domain
  filters. Purpose, pagination, date/year filters and inline fetch are deferred.
  See the [TinyFish reference](docs/technical-reference.en.md#tinyfish-search) for configuration and switching modes.

### Metaso protocol notes

- The [Metaso Search API playground](https://metaso.cn/search-api/playground) documents
  authenticated POST search at `/api/v1/search`.
- Metaso requires an API key (Bearer token). Anonymous access returns HTTP 401.
- Results are read from `webpages`, falling back to `results`, `papers`, `documents`
  or `data`; a usable `link` maps to `url`, otherwise a usable `url` is used (the
  shared http(s) result URL policy applies), `snippet` (or `content` when `snippet`
  is absent) to `text`, and a string `date` to `age`.
- Supports configurable search scope (`webpage`, `document`, `paper`, `image`, `video`, `podcast`).
- Public search caps results at 50 (`resolveResultCount(count, countPolicy)`).

### SerpApi protocol notes

- The [Google Search Engine Results API](https://serpapi.com/search-api) documents
  authenticated GET search at `https://serpapi.com/search`.
- SerpApi requires an API key and has no anonymous path. The key is passed via the `api_key`
  query parameter.
- Only the first page of `organic_results` is mapped: `link` to `url`, `title` to `title`,
  `snippet` to `text`, and string `date` to `age`. Other SERP blocks and hits lacking
  a valid link are ignored; malformed optional snippets become empty text.
- Google deprecated the `num` parameter in September 2025; results are retrieved as returned
  by upstream and locally capped (`resolveResultCount(count, countPolicy)`, at most 10).
- An error-free empty array or `status: "Success"` with `organic_results_state:
  "Fully empty"` returns `[]` and is cached for at most 30 seconds. The latter may
  include SerpApi's empty-result error string. Unexplained errors, unknown statuses
  and null result arrays fail without caching. magpie reports `found nothing` if
  no provider supplies results.
- SerpApi-generated errors omit original exceptions, upstream bodies and request
  URLs. Refusals retain numeric status and validated, normalized `Retry-After` only;
  body cancellation cannot delay the refusal. Redirects are rejected. This policy
  does not control vendor/proxy logs or alter ordinary search result content.
- Supports optional location, country (`gl`), language (`hl`), domain (`googleDomain`),
  and safe-search (`safe`) options with environment variable fallbacks.

### Moonshot and Moonshot CN protocol notes

- The Moonshot Basic search API ([international](https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/api/tools-search.md), [domestic](https://platform.kimi.com/docs/api/tools-search.md)) documents standalone `POST /v1/tools/search` with Bearer authentication. Default endpoints are `https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/tools/search` and `https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/tools/search`.
- Both sites require an API key (`keyOptional: false`). Credentials and console accounts are independent; keys are configured separately and are not interchanged.
- Basic search accepts `text_query` and `limit` (1–20, sized via `resolveResultCount(count, countPolicy)`). The initial release does not expose Pro search, responses API, formula API, or model-integrated search.
- Response payloads must contain a `search_results` array. Results map `url` to `url`, non-empty `title` to `title` (fallback to URL), and string `date` to `age`.
- Results default to snippet text (`content: "snippet"`). When `content: "full"` is selected, requests include `"include_content": true`, and nonblank string `text` is preferred over `snippet` while preserving whitespace and markdown indentation. Both modes retain up to `contentChars` code points (default 4000, 0 disables local truncation) and append `…` when truncating; Magpie still applies its own text limit.
- On HTTP 429, standard `Retry-After` takes precedence, including zero. The fallback `X-RateLimit-Reset` conversion accepts delays of 1–86400 seconds; invalid or excessive values are omitted for host defaults. Official timestamps use Unix seconds; plausible proxy millisecond timestamps are tolerated within the same window. This bound is a local defensive policy, not an upstream quota guarantee; see the [Moonshot reference](docs/technical-reference.en.md#moonshot-search) for conversion rules.
- Official billing applies to HTTP 200 with a non-empty upstream `search_results` array ($0.002/search internationally before applicable taxes, ¥0.01/search domestically). Local filtering or truncation does not reduce that charge. Search rate limits are independent of model RPM/TPM limits.
- Both adapters have passed dummy-key local simulations and Magpie host checks. Successful searches, full text, latency, rate limiting and search quality with real account keys have not been verified on either site.

  cannot fill a short response. Quark warns and ignores a nonempty environment
  domain filter, but under Quark an explicit nonempty `domainFilter` fails configuration.

  validation; use a single bare domain without a scheme, path, list or wildcard.

  string `publish_date` to `age`. Text defaults to 4000 code points plus an
  appended `…` when truncated; 0 keeps all.

  lists without any usable links fail without caching. Explicit empty arrays
  cache for at most 30 seconds. For proxy compatibility, `code` values `0`, `"0"`,

  429 can mean balance/quota exhaustion as well as rate limiting. Requests reject
  redirects and custom URLs are exact endpoints. The site, endpoint, effective
  request parameters, local limit, text budget and credential are hashed together
  to form the cache identity; no raw credential is stored in the cache key.
- Published REST prices: domestic ¥0.01/0.03/0.05/0.05 per use respectively;
  international $0.01 per use. No promise of free empty or failed searches is made.
  Coding Plan MCP is a separate access path and is never used by the `zhipu` or `zai`
  REST adapters.
- Dummy-key tests cover protocol behavior and host scheduling; successful searches,
  filter effects, billing, real account limits and quality with real keys remain

## Adding a provider

1. Check official magpie support and the provider's current API documentation.
2. Implement `execute({ query, count, key, url }, ctx)`. Use the supplied key,
   honor the custom Base URL (exact endpoint across all providers), and cap `count`
   according to the API's limits. If upstream has no count parameter, cap valid results
   locally. Use `configCountPolicy` and `resolveResultCount` so an omitted `resultLimit` follows
   the host count while explicit options and valid environment values remain caps.
   Preserve the legacy fallback only when no valid host count is supplied. Filter
   unusable rows before capping, even when the upstream ignores the requested count.
3. Return `{ title, url, text, age? }` results. Drop entries without a URL and
   entries whose URL does not pass the shared absolute `http:`/`https:` result
   URL policy, and preserve the provider's date string when available.
4. Preserve `ctx.abort` and apply the configured request timeout. Reject HTTP
   redirects and reject queries that normalize to an empty string before fetching. Throw errors
   with a numeric `status` for HTTP refusals and carry `retryAfter` on 429. Use the shared
   `requestResponse`/`requestJSON` reader: ordinary REST bodies are bounded locally at
   16 MiB for success and 64 KiB for failures, so do not call `response.text()` directly.
5. Create settings and cache per plugin instance. Isolate cache entries by
   hashing the final endpoint, credential and all request parameters together.
6. Add optional provider settings with environment fallback and document their
   defaults and canonical names in both technical references. Follow the
   [configuration naming rules](#configuration-naming) below. magpie continues to own API keys.
7. For APIs that support anonymous requests, set `keyOptional: true`, omit empty
   authentication headers and select the documented anonymous endpoint. Keep an
   anonymous 429 cooldown per final endpoint because magpie does not rest empty
   keys. Preserve keyed behavior without silently downgrading failed keys.
8. Register the API by default while preserving the optional `enable`/`disable`
   filters (`disable` wins). Use short IDs for those filters and update the
   registration checks. Set `name` to `<Provider> (magpie-websearch)` and keep
   vendor IDs stable. magpie owns request ordering and its own on/off switches.
9. Add response fixtures and tests for request mapping, custom URLs, cache
   isolation and errors. Cover host counts above 6 and the `fallbackCount` with at
   least 25 valid results, smaller explicit/environment caps, `providerMax` and
   missing-count fallbacks. Exercise canonical `resultLimit` names and legacy
   aliases. Files named `*.test.mjs` in `test/` are discovered by `scripts/test.mjs`
   on both Node and Bun without a shell glob. Run Node, Bun and the magpie host checks.
10. Update the supported-provider table, README, package description and keywords.

### Configuration naming

Environment variable names are defined locally by each adapter; they are not
derived from upstream responses. New settings must follow this convention:

```text
ENV_NAME = UPPER_SNAKE_CASE(provider short ID) + "_" + UPPER_SNAKE_CASE(option name)
```

Use string option names in camelCase, preserving acronym groups such as `TTL`.
Convert hyphens in provider IDs to underscores and uppercase the ID. Convert
option word boundaries to underscores and uppercase the option name:

| Provider short ID | Option | Environment variable |
|---|---|---|
| `moonshot` | `timeout` | `MOONSHOT_TIMEOUT` |
| `moonshot-cn` | `resultLimit` | `MOONSHOT_CN_RESULT_LIMIT` |
| `moonshot-cn` | `cacheTTL` | `MOONSHOT_CN_CACHE_TTL` |
| `moonshot-cn` | `contentChars` | `MOONSHOT_CN_CONTENT_CHARS` |

`configInt` and `configStr` strip the complete option suffix and convert the
remaining prefix to a lowercase ID with hyphens. This produces error fields such
as `moonshot-cn.resultLimit` without changing the environment key used to read values.
Do not prepend an application prefix or introduce an unrelated suffix for new settings.

When retaining an existing environment alias or another naming scheme, explicitly
pass the provider short ID as the final `namespace` argument to either helper.
If the option suffix does not match, automatic inference falls back to the first
environment segment and may lose a multi-part provider ID. The namespace override
only labels errors; it does not rename the environment variable or change configuration
precedence. Add tests for the error field, environment fallback and explicit-option
priority, and document defaults and environment mappings in both technical references.

All search adapters use `resultLimit` / `*_RESULT_LIMIT` for the optional user cap.
`configCountPolicy` returns separate `configuredLimit`, `fallbackCount` and
`providerMax` fields. Declare compatibility aliases through `legacyOption` and
`legacyEnv`: the default aliases are `maxResults` / `*_MAX_RESULTS`, while Querit
uses `count` / `QUERIT_COUNT`. New options beat old options; either beats environment
values, where the new nonblank name beats its alias. Keep protocol fields such as
Linkup's `maxResults` and Querit's upstream `count` unchanged.

During the pause it returns a 429 without fetching, allowing magpie to try the next configured API. Cached results remain usable, and supplying a key bypasses the anonymous pause. Cooldowns are kept in memory per plugin instance, reset when the host reloads, and remain active even when `cacheTTL` is zero. ## Parallel search Parallel has two access paths, selected by the key magpie supplies: | Access | Default endpoint | Request | |---|---|---| | Anonymous (empty key) | `https://mcp.parallel.ai/mcp` | POST JSON-RPC `tools/call`, tool `web_search` | | With a key | `https://api.parallel.ai/v1/search` | POST with `x-api-key` and nested `advanced_settings` | Anonymous requests directly call `web_search` without a session handshake. The plugin reads JSON or SSE responses, checks JSON-RPC and tool errors, then extracts search results from structured content or text content parts. Keyed requests use the GA `/v1/search` endpoint with `x-api-key`. Both paths accept a normalized query of 1–200 characters (Parallel's keyword query limit). Parallel's MCP server defaults to `fast` mode. If `parallel.mode` is configured to another mode (`turbo`, `basic` or `advanced`), anonymous requests fail before fetching with an error reminding you to add a key. With a key, all four modes are supported on REST. Parallel's public search caps results at 20. The plugin requests at most 20 results on REST and caps valid results locally to magpie's count and `parallel.resultLimit`. `text` joins `excerpts` with `\n\n`; it retains up to `parallel.contentChars` code points (default 4000, `0` keeps all returned text) and appends `…` when truncated. `publish_date` preserves the original date string as `age`. Anonymous access was verified on **2026-11-04** against the official MCP endpoint: keyless `tools/call` returned HTTP 200 with search results for English and Chinese queries. A configured key always selects REST, including when it is invalid or exhausted; there is no automatic downgrade to MCP. A custom endpoint is used as the exact destination for either protocol (for example, `/mcp` anonymously or your proxy's search endpoint with a key). ## TinyFish search TinyFish has two access paths, selected by the key magpie supplies: | Access | Default endpoint | Request | |---|---|---| | Anonymous (empty key) | `https://agent.tinyfish.ai/mcp` | POST JSON-RPC `tools/call`, tool `search`, header `X-TinyFish-Access-Mode: keyless` | | With a key | `https://api.search.tinyfish.ai/` | GET with URL-encoded search parameters, header `X-API-Key` | Anonymous requests directly call the search tool without a session handshake. The plugin reads either JSON or SSE responses, checks JSON-RPC and tool errors, then extracts the search JSON from structured content or a text content part. REST requests have no body. Both paths accept a normalized query of 1–2000 characters. Neither sends a result-count parameter: TinyFish returns one page, then the plugin drops URL-less entries and caps valid results to magpie's requested count and `tinyfish.resultLimit`. It does not fetch more pages to fill a short response. `text` is the search snippet; `age` preserves `date`, including human-readable dates. A paper's numeric `year` is not converted to a date. Both paths support the configured location, language, domain filters, and `web` or `news` searches. `research_paper` requires a key; using it anonymously reports an error before making a request. Omitted location/language are resolved by TinyFish: one can determine the other, and omitting both defaults to US/en. The plugin does not infer them from the query. Purpose, pagination, date/year filters, thumbnails and inline page fetching are not exposed as plugin options. For example, use Chinese-language news search with a local cap of four results: ```sh magpie plugin options magpie-websearch '{"tinyfish":{"language":"zh","domainType":"news","resultLimit":4}}' ``` Anonymous access was verified on **2026-11-04** against the official MCP endpoint: keyless `tools/call` returned HTTP 200 with search results, and `tools/list` advertised `web`/`news` plus location, language and domain filtering. The same MCP call without the keyless header returned 401. The REST endpoint returned 401 without an API key, even with that header. The [REST reference](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/search-api/reference.md) documents API keys; the [MCP guide](https://docs.tinyfish.ai/mcp-integration/index.md) primarily documents OAuth and does not fully describe this anonymous route. This is observed support, not a guarantee of permanent anonymous access. Its precise quota is not documented here; do not assume it shares authenticated account limits. HTTP 429 uses the anonymous cooldown described above. JSON-RPC codes and tool-error text are not treated as HTTP status codes. The adapter also passed a live anonymous search against that endpoint. Keyed REST success and MCP SSE parsing were verified against a local fake service, including through the magpie host; a successful REST search with a real account key has not been verified. A configured key always selects REST, including when it is invalid or exhausted; there is no automatic downgrade to MCP. See [Anonymous search and rate limits](#anonymous-search) for switching a saved keyed entry back to anonymous access. A custom endpoint must match the selected protocol, for example `/proxy/mcp` anonymously or `/proxy/search` with a key; neither address is rewritten. ## SerpApi search SerpApi integrates with Google's search engine via SerpApi's Google Search API: - **Protocol**: GET requests to `https://serpapi.com/search` with URL-encoded query parameters and authentication via `api_key`. - **Sensitive Error Protection**: Network, HTTP, parsing and status errors use fixed descriptions and necessary status codes, without retaining original exceptions, response bodies, request URLs or an underlying `cause`. Requests do not follow redirects. This protects plugin-generated errors and diagnostics; it cannot control server or proxy logs and does not rewrite normal web result content. - **Organic Results & Local Capping**: Only `organic_results` items with valid links are retained. Because Google deprecated the `num` parameter in September 2025, results are retrieved per page and capped locally (`serpapi.resultLimit`). - **Empty Result Handling**: An error-free empty array, or `status: "Success"` with `organic_results_state: "Fully empty"`, returns `[]`; the latter may contain SerpApi's empty-result error string. Null result fields, unknown statuses and unexplained errors fail without caching. Valid empty results are cached for at most 30 seconds; `cacheTTL: 0` disables plugin caching. When no other results are available, magpie reports `found nothing`. - **Optional Knobs**: Supports configuring country (`gl`), interface language (`hl`), location (`location`), Google domain (`googleDomain`), and safe search (`safe`) with environment variable fallbacks. `hl` controls interface language and `gl` is a country preference; neither strictly restricts result language or source country. The adapter fetches one page without automatic pagination. The 1–10 `resultLimit` range is a local plugin cap, and fewer results may be returned. Disabling plugin caching does not disable SerpApi's server cache. Under the [official billing rules](https://serpapi.com/pricing), successful empty searches can count toward quota; reducing the local cap does not reduce the charge for a search. ## Moonshot and Moonshot CN search Moonshot provides two independent Basic web search endpoints: | Site | Adapter ID | Default endpoint | Console & API keys | |---|---|---|---| | International | `moonshot` | `https://api.moonshot.ai/v1/tools/search` | `https://platform.kimi.ai/console/api-keys` | | Domestic (China) | `moonshot-cn` | `https://api.moonshot.cn/v1/tools/search` | `https://platform.kimi.com/console/api-keys` | - **Protocol and Request Constraints**: Standalone Basic search API over `POST` JSON with Bearer authentication and `redirect: "error"`. Snippet requests contain `text_query` and `limit` (1–20, sized via `resolveResultCount(count, countPolicy)`); full-text requests also send `include_content: true`. Pro search, standalone fetch, Responses API, Formula API and model-integrated search are not exposed; the server-side `timeout_seconds` parameter is omitted. - **Content Mode and Truncation**: Defaults to snippet mode (`content: "snippet"`), omitting `include_content` from the request and reading `snippet`. In full-text mode (`content: "full"`), requests include `"include_content": true`, and valid `text` is preferred over `snippet` while preserving whitespace and indentation. Both modes retain up to `contentChars` code points (default 4000, `0` disables local truncation) and append `…` when truncating, without splitting emoji surrogate pairs. Note that Magpie applies its own 1500-byte cap downstream. - **Result Processing**: Upstream must return an object with a `search_results` array. Entries lacking valid URLs or object shape are dropped; if upstream returns items but none are valid, a structural error is raised instead of caching an empty result. `title` falls back to the URL, a …[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]… :"deep","resultLimit":4}}' ``` An unknown ID is logged and ignored. An explicit `enable` list containing no known IDs registers no APIs and logs a warning. A filter that is not an array is logged and ignored; malformed per-provider settings instead fail loading as described under [Full configuration reference](#configuration). These filters control registration. magpie's Web search switches independently control whether a registered API is asked, keeping its key and place in the list when switched off. You can use those switches without setting either filter. To remove all saved plugin options, including provider overrides and filters: ```sh magpie plugin options magpie-websearch off ``` All twenty-one APIs are registered again. Provider settings use environment values when present, otherwise their defaults. To remove only the filters, save a complete options object containing the provider settings you want to keep. ## Development and local tests For new provider settings, name environment variables as the uppercase underscore form of the provider short ID, followed by `_` and the uppercase underscore form of the option name. For example, `moonshot-cn.resultLimit` maps to `MOONSHOT_CN_RESULT_LIMIT`, and `cacheTTL` maps to the `CACHE_TTL` suffix. Option names must be strings in camelCase; adapters define these names locally. Parse result limits with `configCountPolicy`; declare their compatibility names through `legacyOption` and `legacyEnv`. Other shared helpers strip the complete option suffix to label errors; for retained environment aliases, pass the provider short ID as `namespace`. See the [provider integration rules](../PROVIDERS.md#configuration-naming) for details. Reuse `truncateCodePoints(text, limit)` for text budgets. Callers supply a string and a validated nonnegative integer; the function does not validate types, trim whitespace or normalize text. 0 keeps all text; truncation retains the first N code points and appends `…`.
